p:cNvPr.descr: An image illustrating the regulation of pyruvate kinase. In the middle of the image is a blue oval, entitled pyruvate kinase L/M. Just to the left of the oval is a dashed vertical line going up and dashed vertical line going down. The left side of the image is entitled "liver only." The right side of the line is entitled "All glycolytic tissues, including liver."A curved arrow goes left to another blue oval entitled pyruvate kinase L (inactive). This oval has a black "P" in a red circle shooting off at the top left. The pyruvate kinase L oval has a curved arrow from the bottom pointing right back to the pyruvate kinase L/M oval. Above the curved arrow going from pyruvate kinase L/M to pyruvate kinase L is another inversed curved arrow that goes from ATP to ADP. In the middle is PKA (in blue). Directly above PKA is a green rectangle in a cirlce that has a dashed arrow pointing to it entitled glucagon. An arrow from the blue pyruvate kinase L/M oval points right to a curved arrow that starts with ADP and points to ATP. Above that arrow, F16BP has reversible arrows pointing to PEP. In the middle of those arrows, it says, "6 steps." F16BP also has a dashed arrow first moving right, then down, then left pointing to a green rectangle in a circle. Below that rectangle is a red X in a circle that has a dashed arrow pointing to it from the right entitled ATP, acetyl-CoA, long-chain fatty acids. Below that red X in a circle is another red X in a circle. From the PEP mentioned above is one solid arrow pointing down to pyruvate, which then has reversible arrows pointing to alanine. In the middle of those arrows, it says, "transamination." From alanaline, a dashed arrow first points right, then up, then left to the second red X in a circle mentioned above.
